statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ extended its restart range to 29,530.50-29,621.75 by tagging a new session high near 29,621.75, then handed the whole extension back and last quoted around 29,565-29,582. An upside break that is fully retraced inside the same hour is the clearest available evidence against a no-retracement path, so Tail stays at the low-band floor. Stress ticks to 55 on a ten-year yield near 4.784%, a 58% market-implied probability of a Federal Reserve hike on 16 September, and a Hormuz disruption that Tehran has signalled it will formalise with a restricted zone.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the early Labor Day futures halt, and secondarily in the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, rather than across the whole outlook. Every forecast hour maps below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures make a new restart high near 29,622 and give it all back within the hour as a 2% Nikkei rally and a near-10% weekly oil gain fail to produce directional structure
body:
The most important observation this hour is a completed retracement. NQ front-month extended the Sunday restart range to 29,530.50-29,621.75, roughly 91 points or 0.31%, by printing a new session high near 29,621.75 that had not existed an hour earlier. It then returned the entire extension and last quoted between 29,565.25 and 29,582.00 depending on venue, essentially unchanged on the session at +0.06% to +0.14%. A break that fails and mean-reverts inside a single hour is the direct opposite of the repeated-extension-after-failed-retracement pattern that overwhelms a reverse or grid strategy, and it is why Tail sits at the low-band floor rather than carrying a thin-book premium.

The regional divergence widened rather than closed. Japan's Nikkei rebounded 2.0% and South Korea rallied 3.0%, while the broader Topix managed only 0.8% and MSCI's Asia-Pacific-ex-Japan index added 0.9%. That is a narrow, semiconductor-and-memory-led bid rather than a broad risk impulse, and NQ declined to follow any of it. Reuters characterised S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures as a fraction lower on thin holiday turnover during the same window. An index that neither tracks a 2% regional technology rally nor sells off against it is rotating, and rotation is the environment in which mean reversion works.

Energy remains the live but chronic channel. WTI trades near 92.13 and Brent near 96.87, up about 0.7% and 0.6%, after a week in which WTI gained close to 10% and Brent 7.8%. US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday, including one off Kharg Island, after the Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at two US Navy vessels, and Tehran has signalled it will announce a restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz in the coming days. Kpler data show an average of ten commodity ships transiting the strait per day over the past ten days, the lowest since May. Separately, seven OPEC+ producers left October quotas unchanged at about 31.01 million barrels per day at a virtual meeting on 6 September, with the next review on 4 October. This is a severe but already-priced supply disruption rather than a fresh discontinuity, which is why it supports Stress and not Tail.

The rate backdrop firmed. Ten-year Treasury yields sit near 4.7840%, close to their highest since late 2023, with commentary framing a move toward 5.0% as contingent on an elevated CPI print. Following Friday's upbeat payrolls report, markets price a 58% probability of a Federal Reserve hike at the 16 September meeting and 70% for a move by October. The H.15 release still shows the two-year at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77% as of 3 September, and Friday's VIX close of 14.53 is low in absolute terms. Friday's Nasdaq internals were split rather than aligned: the semiconductor complex was uniformly higher, led by Micron and AMD, while five of eight megacaps fell and Tesla dropped almost 6%. No cross-asset alignment of the kind that amplifies Tail is present.

Today is Labor Day. US cash equity and Treasury markets are closed, and CME equity index futures trade a shortened session that halts at 17:00 UTC with no Monday settlement published, reopening at 22:00 UTC for the Tuesday trade date. The narrow danger window stays at 15:00 to 17:00 UTC, covering the European cash close into that hard deadline, because a squeeze into a fixed halt in an already thin book remains the most plausible unrepaired-move mechanism in this outlook. It is a conditional scenario, not an observation.

The week is back-loaded and empty today. August PPI and jobless claims arrive on Thursday 10 September and August CPI on Friday 11 September, the last inflation reading before the 15-16 September FOMC decision, with the Fed already in its pre-meeting communications blackout. Under the standing calibration, event importance and forecast dispersion of that kind inform Stress and Confidence rather than Tail, and none of those events falls inside this 24-hour outlook.

Shared delayed cross-asset context collected at 01:20 UTC is now about two hours old and therefore past its freshness threshold, so this assessment rests on independently verified live sources; where the two overlap they agree on a flat index-futures complex, contained rate futures and firmer crude.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday session, mapping to EA_ON and green in every available hour, then stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart to carry reopen-gap risk before easing to 6 and back to 5 once the restart proved orderly. Stress ran from 56 down to a 52 low at 07:00 UTC, drifted up through a 55-58 band as Sunday's geopolitical flow accumulated, peaked at 60 at 20:00 UTC, then eased to 57, 56, 55 and 54 after the reopen. Dominant mode was normal in every available hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the rest of the Asian session, a European session traded against closed US cash equity and Treasury markets on Labor Day, a shortened futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, and the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band in every hour: 5 through the Asian hours now that a new session high has been made and fully retraced, 6 across the Asian-to-European handover and pre-open, 7 from the European cash open through the mid-morning where the weekend Iran and OPEC+ headlines first meet real depth without a US cash backstop, 6 through the holiday-thinned midday, 7 across the notional US open and early afternoon, 8 as the danger window opens at the European cash close and a peak of 9 in the final hour before the early halt, the closed-venue floor of 5 while futures are shut, then 8 at the Tuesday restart easing to 7 and 6. Conditional Stress tracks the same shape between 53 and 58, and Confidence decays from 86 to 74 as the assessment ages away from its evidence cutoff.
